subject: Clarifying: No‑training Commitment & Retention Windows for Medicore
messages:
From: Gina Russo <gina.russo@medicore.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Medicore Legal <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Nov 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Quick confirmation on training + retention windows

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Medicore is excited about the latency and the dedicated options. Our security team needs a short, plain‑language confirmation on two points before we proceed: 1) "Do you train your models on customer data?" and 2) "What are the practical retention windows for request logs, cached KV state, and backup snapshots?"

We need something we can share with Legal and the InfoSec reviewer that isn't legalese. If you can include what data may persist in backups or logs, how long, and whether those artifacts could be used for model training under any circumstance, that would be perfect.

Gina Russo
Director of Cloud Integrations
Medicore Health

P.S. If you have a short FAQ or a one‑pager, please attach.
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Gina Russo <gina.russo@medicore.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 01 Nov 2028 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation on training + retention windows

Hi Gina — appreciate the clear ask and the fast review loop. Short answer up front: we do not train any models on customer data that you send to the Redwood inference API. That is a standing, default commitment for our hosted and Dedicated offerings unless a separate opt‑in program is explicitly agreed.

High level bullets for your team: 
- No training: Customer text, prompts, and generation outputs are not used to update or fine‑tune Redwood models.
- Caching & KV: We may cache ephemeral prefixes and KV cache to accelerate active sessions. These caches live only in memory-backed or local node storage and are purged per session/policy (more below).
- Logs & backups: Operational logs (request id, timestamps, basic metadata) are retained for operational and billing reasons. Backups and snapshots are encrypted and retained per configured retention windows.

I've looped in Neha (Legal) and Grace (Ops) to add retention numbers and call out any edge cases (backups, disaster recovery, logs used for debugging). Attaching our short FAQ that covers these points.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-data-retention-FAQ.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 02 Nov 2028 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick confirmation on training + retention windows

Gina — adding the legal/controls detail you can drop into Medicore's review docs. I kept this summary non‑technical so Legal can paste it into the risk memo.

1) Training policy (short):
- Redwood does not use customer inference requests, prompts, or outputs to train, fine‑tune, or update any production or research models by default.
- Any deviation (participation in a training/feedback program) requires an explicit, written opt‑in and a separate agreement describing scope, duration, and compensation.

2) Operational telemetry & logs:
- Request metadata (request_id, timestamp, model_id, region) retained for 90 days by default for debugging, billing reconciliation, and abuse monitoring.
- Optional extended retention up to 7 years is available under enterprise contracts / compliance add‑ons (we surface this as a toggle in Dedicated/Private contracts).

3) Caching, KV, and ephemeral storage:
- KV cache and any in‑flight caches exist to support low‑latency decoding. They are node‑local and are cleared on session end or after 24 hours of inactivity by default.
- Customers can configure shorter TTLs or disable caching in Dedicated and Private deployments.

4) Backups and snapshots:
- Persistent backups (for stateful services we run) are encrypted at rest and retained for a default of 30 days.
- For Dedicated customers with stronger requirements we can configure backup retention, and we provide deletion/rotation schedules as part of onboarding.

5) Model training risk/assurance: 
- We do not and will not feed customer request data into our model training pipelines without written consent.
- Logs and backups are not connected to training pipelines; the training infrastructure is segregated from the inference telemetry stores.

6) Evidence & attestations:
- See attached: Medicore non‑training acknowledgment template (you can sign and return).
- We can provide an addendum to the SLA specifying retention windows and an audit clause for an enterprise engagement.

If Medicore Legal has specific language they prefer, we can review and sign an acknowledgment (SLA amendment).

—Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

2) In a disaster recovery restore from a snapshot, could customer payloads be written back into live nodes where they might be exposed to other tenant traffic before eviction?

Hi Gina — operational answers below, keeping them concise for InfoSec: 

1) Backups & encryption:
- Backups may include request payloads only for stateful features where the payload is explicitly persisted (e.g., conversation history stored via the Redwood Conversations API). For stateless inference requests we do not persist raw payloads in backups.
- All backups are encrypted at rest with customer‑separated encryption keys for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted customers we use KMS with RBAC and can provide key‑holder details in the contract.

2) DR restores & tenant isolation:
- Restore processes target an isolated staging environment by default. Restored data is validated and sanitized before being mounted to production. We do not directly restore snapshots into shared live nodes that serve other tenants.
- For enterprise customers we offer a dedicated restore lane that restores into customer‑scoped infrastructure.

3) Practical mitigations you can request in the order form:
- Disable long‑term backups for specific projects; set backup TTL to 0.
- Shorten KV and cache TTL (e.g., 1 hour or session only).
- Request that all snapshots with customer payloads be stored with a Medicore‑managed CMK (customer master key) for additional control.

If useful I can join your call with InfoSec and Medicore Legal tomorrow morning — Tessa/Neha, happy to join.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Redwood Inference
